Retrieved via Exa web_fetch. ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 17, 2026 (republished by Kyiv Post; original at understandingwar.org).

Key Takeaways:
- The Russian Ministry of Defense (MoD) appears committed to optimizing Russian forces for continued POSITIONAL WARFARE in Ukraine — not for the mechanized manoeuvre required to make rapid, large-scale gains.
- Russia's prioritization of its war efforts and suboptimal economic policies are reportedly triggering a broader ECONOMIC DECLINE in Russia.
- A Russian state-affiliated polling center recorded one of the SHARPEST DROPS in President Vladimir Putin's approval ratings since the start of the war, following several months of steady decline.
- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced further personnel changes within the Ukrainian government on July 17.
- Russia launched one Kh-31P anti-radar missile, seven Kh-59/69 guided missiles, and 130 drones against Ukraine overnight.
- Neither Ukrainian nor Russian forces made confirmed advances on July 17.

Related Kyiv Post items (same page, timestamped ~18 July): Drones struck Russian-occupied Crimea (fire near Gvardeyskoye airfield); Kyiv placed on alert twice overnight over ballistic missile threat; Zelensky offered former Interior Minister Klymenko a National Security and Defense Council role.
